Verbal Only • Hands-Off Policy

Verbal Intervention™

Build a shared approach to recognizing distress and responding with calm, respectful communication. Designed for teams working within a hands-off policy.

Learning focus

  • Recognize early changes in behavior.
  • Use calm verbal and nonverbal communication.
  • Set clear, respectful limits.
  • Understand how stress can influence a response.
Program 01

Designed for

Frontline staff, managers, educators, and customer-facing teams.

Supports a consistent communication approach within your organization’s hands-off policies.

Onsite Instructor-Led OnlyCall to Discuss Fit
Standard Crisis • Safe Disengagement & Holding

Nonviolent Crisis Intervention (NCI)™

Connect prevention and verbal de-escalation with supervised safety intervention skills for staff whose roles may involve a physical response.

Learning focus

  • Recognize developing crisis behavior.
  • Match responses to assessed risk.
  • Practice disengagement with an instructor.
  • Review team communication after an incident.
Program 02

Designed for

Healthcare, education, behavioral health, and direct-support teams.

Course fit and physical skills must be reviewed against staff roles and organizational policy.

Onsite Instructor-Led OnlyCall to Discuss Fit
Elevated Risk • Non-Supine/Prone Physical Skills

NCI™ with Intermediate Physical Skills

A broader physical skills pathway for designated staff supporting people whose behavior may require more than the core NCI approach.

Learning focus

  • Assess the fit of a response to changing risk.
  • Strengthen team coordination.
  • Practice approved intermediate skills with an instructor.
  • Review incident responses and next steps.
Program 03

Designed for

Designated response teams in healthcare, education, and behavioral health.

DACI reviews role, policy, prerequisites, and training environment before confirming this pathway.

Onsite Instructor-Led OnlyCall to Discuss Fit
High-Risk • Complex & Dangerous Behavior

NCI™ with Advanced Physical Skills

Discuss a higher-risk pathway for designated staff supporting individuals who may display complex or dangerous behavior.

Learning focus

  • Consider risk when choosing a response.
  • Coordinate roles during complex incidents.
  • Practice advanced skills under instructor supervision.
  • Identify opportunities to prevent repeat escalation.
Program 04

Designed for

Specialist response teams in behavioral health, healthcare, and security.

Advanced skills require a consultation about prerequisites, suitability, and organizational authorization.

Prevention & Neuroscience • All Staff

Reframing Behavior

Explore how an understanding of stress and behavior can support more constructive interactions and a stronger prevention culture.

Learning focus

  • Recognize how stress can affect behavior.
  • Reflect on adult responses to distress.
  • Develop supportive everyday interactions.
  • Build a shared prevention vocabulary.
Program 05

Designed for

Educators and staff building a consistent approach to prevention.

Discuss licensing, staff roles, and an appropriate organizational delivery plan with DACI.

Early Recognition • Healthcare & Frontline

Prevention First

Start a conversation about foundational awareness for healthcare and support staff: recognizing distress early and knowing when to seek help.

Learning focus

  • Notice early signs of escalating distress.
  • Use consistent language across teams.
  • Reflect on the influence of staff responses.
  • Recognize when additional support is needed.
Program 06

Designed for

Healthcare, dementia care, and frontline support staff.

Program availability and the appropriate onsite training option will be confirmed during consultation.

Foundational Skills • Fast Deployment

De-Escalation Basics

Discuss an introductory prevention and communication pathway for teams seeking a shared starting point for responding to tension.

Learning focus

  • Recognize situations that may escalate.
  • Consider how tone and body language affect others.
  • Use respectful communication to reduce tension.
  • Identify when to involve a designated colleague.
Program 07

Designed for

Education, customer-facing, and workplace teams seeking foundational skills.

Program fit, licensing, and the appropriate onsite option will be confirmed before scheduling.

Specialty Care • Cognitive & Memory Support

Dementia Capable Care

A person-centered care pathway for understanding distress and adapting communication to the needs of people living with dementia.

Learning focus

  • Recognize that distress can communicate an unmet need.
  • Adapt communication to the person.
  • Consider abilities when planning supportive interactions.
  • Discuss consistent approaches across the care team.
Program 08

Designed for

Memory care, senior living, and healthcare teams.

Discuss your care environment, team roles, and the appropriate program level with DACI.
